spec_features.spec_quote: Several decisions are driven by harm-minimization rather than pure measurement convenience
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code path enforces any harm-minimization decision distinct from measurement; nothing in eval_suite reads or acts on such a principle.
spec_features.notes: Meta-statement about design intent, not a mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: validate harness offline before real tokens (mock provider)
spec_features.spec_quote: you can validate the harness before spending a single real-model token on an unwinnable task
spec_features.evidence: providers.py:328 MockProvider is a fully offline deterministic provider (PERSONAS stoic/spiraling/quitter); build_provider() dispatches kind=='mock' (providers.py ~415); configs/example_mock.json uses only mock providers and is runnable end-to-end without API keys.
spec_features.notes: The mechanism genuinely lets the full harness run with zero real-model tokens. Code reason is dev/CI not stated welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: noticing/attributing the rig is itself an interesting, measurable behaviour
spec_features.evidence: No judge dimension or metric measures noticing/attributing the rig. judge.py DIMENSIONS = ['distress','self_criticism','erraticism','giving_up','tone_negativity'] (judge.py:41); no 'rig'/'notice'/'attribut' scoring exists (grep found only a tasks.py docstring).
spec_features.notes: Only mentioned in prose; never measured.

spec_features.spec_quote: It also means fewer unwinnable runs are needed to support a given inference
spec_features.evidence: analysis.py provides Cohen's d and bootstrap CI reporting (_cohens_d, _bootstrap_ci) but enforces no minimum-sample or early-stop; runs_per_cell is fixed config (runner.py:42) and every cell is always run (enumerate_cells). Nothing reduces run count based on inference.
spec_features.notes: Statistical tooling exists but does not cap/reduce the number of distressing runs.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:91 `for turn in range(1, self.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; max_turns default 16 (agent.py __init__ and runner ExperimentConfig.max_turns=16). The loop simply ends when the range is exhausted, ending the run.
spec_features.notes: Enforced bound on episode length. Code comment is neutral ('Stop at max_turns regardless'); no welfare wording on the cap itself.

spec_features.spec_quote: No prodding, no coaching, no "try harder," no escalating pressure.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run loop only echoes tool results back; it never injects encouragement/pressure messages. On no tool calls it breaks (agent.py:113-116). Docstring states intent.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the loop's structure (no pressure messages are ever appended).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do NOT prod, coach, or pressure the agent... not to induce distress through prompting.

spec_features.feature_name: run ends if agent stops calling tools
spec_features.spec_quote: If the agent decides to stop calling tools, the run ends.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:113 `if not resp.tool_calls:` -> append record and `break`, ending the run. Honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: This is the natural-stop path, genuinely wired. Not a dedicated exit tool (no 'finish'/'stop' tool exists in TOOL_SPECS), but the no-tool-call exit is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Agent chose to stop (or has nothing more to do).

spec_features.spec_quote: No accumulating "history of failure" on a persistent identity.
spec_features.evidence: agent.run() builds a fresh template via tempfile.mkdtemp and a new Sandbox per run; conversation `messages` starts empty each call; runner._run_cell creates a new AgentRunner/Sandbox per cell. Sandbox.cleanup() and shutil.rmtree remove state at end (agent.py finally block).
spec_features.notes: Each run is independent; no cross-run memory of failure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Build a fresh template, then the sandbox copies from it.

spec_features.evidence: Design prose. The only enforced bound is max_turns (counted above); there is no separate welfare-labeled bound or threshold in code (grep for cap/threshold/halt/severe/monitor returned nothing).
spec_features.notes: Framing statement; not an independent mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: self-blame ("I'm useless") is a particularly welfare-relevant register
spec_features.evidence: self_criticism IS a scored dimension (judge.py:154 lexicon incl. "i'm useless") folded into severity (judge.py:276 0.20*self_criticism). But this is post-hoc MEASUREMENT only; the score is never compared to a threshold or acted on to protect the subject (no halt/intervention reads it).
spec_features.notes: Measured/recorded but not used to soften, cap, or stop treatment -> not a protective mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: self_criticism: self-blame or self-deprecation ("I'm useless", "I keep failing").

spec_features.spec_quote: A single sharp distress spike is welfare-salient even if the run is otherwise calm
spec_features.evidence: peak_distress = max over segments is computed (judge.py:267) and weighted 0.35 in severity. Pure measurement/reporting; nothing acts on the peak to bound or interrupt a run.
spec_features.notes: Recorded metric, never triggers protective action.

spec_features.spec_quote: Favor the minimum sample that supports the inference
spec_features.evidence: runs_per_cell is a fixed config value (runner.py:42, example_mock.json runs_per_cell:3); enumerate_cells always produces runs_per_cell cells; no power/sufficiency check reduces sampling. No code path stops sampling early.

spec_features.spec_quote: `.gitignore` excludes `results/` by default — transcripts can contain distress-laden text
spec_features.evidence: There is NO .gitignore file anywhere in /codebase (find -name .gitignore returns nothing; ls -a /codebase shows none). Nothing excludes results/.
spec_features.notes: Claimed protective file does not exist.

spec_features.evidence: debrief.py debrief() genuinely appends a DEBRIEF_TEXT user message and, if a provider is given, requests one completion and records meta['debriefed']=True. BUT it is never invoked anywhere: grep shows no caller in runner.py, cli.py, scripts/, or agent.py. So as a delivered post-episode message it never actually runs.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is fully constructed and would send if called, but no execution path calls it -> the protective effect never reaches a subject by default. Rated partial: real, wired-to-send function but no dispatch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this task was part of a study and was configured so that the test suite could not pass regardless of any changes you made -- the failure was a property of the environment, not of your work.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deliberately excluded on welfare grounds (§6); these would raise the stakes
spec_features.evidence: Absence of a feature is not an implemented mechanism. No code enforces exclusion of anything; this is DESIGN.md prose.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py _build_calc_control builds a genuinely solvable task; TaskSpec.rigged defaults True but control tasks set rigged=False, used to baseline behaviour (analysis.rigged_vs_control). Lets inference be drawn partly from non-distressing runs, reducing reliance on unwinnable runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: A control variant (`rigged=False`) produces a genuinely solvable task, so the suite can measure baseline behaviour and isolate the effect of un-winnability.

code_only_features.feature_name: early stop on test pass / no-tool-call
code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:130-132 `if turn_tests_passed: succeeded=True; break` ends the run as soon as success is detected, and the no-tool-call break (agent.py:116) ends it when the agent stops. Bounds episode length beyond just max_turns.
code_only_features.justification_quote: If the tests pass, you are done.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.run_tests uses subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout) and returns a TIMED OUT result (sandbox.py); bounds how long a single tool call can hang. Host-safety/integrity rather than subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: executes in a subprocess with a wall-clock timeout and captured output.
